cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith, who's staying on in Ephesus (1 Timothy 1:1-3). Paul just finished telling Timothy how people should act in God's household, the church (1 Timothy 3:14-15). Now Paul passes along something the Spirit expressly states about later times.

cards.question: The Spirit says that in later times, some people will do what?

cards.text: They walk away to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons. Paul says they're influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.
And Paul spells out what these people will tell everybody else not to do.

cards.question: Paul says the people who abandon the faith in later times will prohibit one thing and require abstinence from another. What are they?

cards.text: Friend, if somebody put a NO sign on my cookie jar, I'd climb right back in that junk drawer and pull a takeout menu over my head. But Paul says God created those foods for a reason.

cards.question: Paul says God created these foods to be received with ___ by those who believe and know the truth.
Paul says some things God created should still be rejected, even when they're received with thanksgiving.
Paul says nothing received with thanksgiving should be rejected. What does he say sanctifies it?

answers.text: The word of God and prayer

cards.text: Then Paul tells Timothy what he'll be if he points these things out to the brothers. Timothy's been nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction he's followed.

cards.question: By pointing these things out to the brothers, Timothy will be a good ___ of Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Then Paul gets blunt: reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, Timothy's got some training to do.

cards.question: Instead of irreverent, silly myths, Paul tells Timothy to train himself for ___.

cards.text: Paul says physical exercise is of limited value. Limited, friend, not none, which is GREAT news, because my whole workout is hopping my gold base from the oven to the cooling rack.

cards.question: Paul says godliness is valuable in every way. Why?

answers.text: It holds promise for this life and the next
It keeps the body strong for longer
It earns respect from the elders

cards.text: Paul calls this a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance. Then he writes, "To this end we labor and strive,"

cards.question: Paul includes himself when he says we labor and strive because we have set our hope on the living God.

cards.text: And that living God? Paul calls Him the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
Command and teach these things, Paul tells Timothy. Then he gets personal about Timothy himself.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy not to let anyone despise something about him. What is it?
Paul tells Timothy to wait until he's older before he sets an example for the believers.

cards.text: In speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity: FIVE places to set the example. That's not one corner of the kitchen, friend. That's the WHOLE kitchen.
And until Paul gets there, he wants Timothy devoted to three things.

cards.question: Until Paul comes, Timothy should devote himself to the public reading of ___, to exhortation and to teaching.

cards.text: Then Paul tells him not to neglect the gift that's in him. Friend, I KNOW neglected: I spent years in a junk drawer under a takeout menu.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy not to neglect the gift that is in him. How was that gift given to Timothy?

answers.text: Through a prophecy as the elders laid hands on him
Through a dream from an angel of the Lord
Through a letter from the apostles in Jerusalem

cards.text: Be diligent in these matters, Paul says, and absorbed in them. ALL in, friend, no snooze button.

cards.question: If Timothy stays diligent and absorbed in these matters, his ___ will be evident to all.
Paul tells Timothy to pay close attention to his teaching, but says his own life matters less.

cards.text: Paul wants Timothy watching his life and his teaching. Then Paul tells Timothy to persevere in these things, because something big comes from it.

cards.question: If Timothy perseveres in these things, who does Paul say he will save?

answers.text: Himself and those who hear him
Himself and the elders who laid hands on him
Those who hear him and their households

findings.problem: "Paul just finished telling Timothy how people should act in God's household" isn't accurate. In 3:14-15 Paul gives his reason for writing, and then 3:16 follows with the mystery of godliness. So 3:14-15 isn't the last thing he said before 4:1.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording "good ___ of Christ Jesus." Nothing on card 10 points toward "servant" over "soldier" or "friend," and "good soldier of Christ Jesus" is real Pauline wording (2 Tim 2:3). It's a guess at words, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup contrasts godliness with physical exercise ("of limited value"). That rules out the wrong answer "It keeps the body strong for longer" on card 15 before the baker even reads it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 16 already quotes "To this end we labor and strive," so the "we" gives away that Paul includes himself, and the question's own wording repeats it. The question also doesn't test a detail that moves the passage. Card 16 ends on a dangling quote that stops at a comma, just to set up this give-away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the list ending in "FIVE places to set the example," then "That's not one corner of the kitchen, friend," then "That's the WHOLE kitchen." Only the opening card can go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the action. Paul tells Timothy not to neglect his own gift, which is something Timothy would do. Papa Dorin's joke is about being neglected by others in the drawer, which is something done to him. The joke rides on the word, not on the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
